$comment: THE ONE DECLARATION OF WHAT A FLASHABLE PI TERMINAL IMAGE CONTAINS.
Mirrors infra/kitluy-store-hub-image/runtime-manifest.json, and exists for
the same reason: the terminal tree had two build paths that disagreed, and
nothing reconciled them. A component declared here and not packaged fails
the build; a component packaged and not declared is invisible to the tests.
Three consumers read this file, which is what keeps them from drifting:
1. scripts/package-bootstrap-runtime.sh -- packages what is declared here
2. test/image-contents.test.sh          -- inspects a BUILT rootfs for it
3. test/systemd-runtime.test.sh         -- cross-checks enablement
FACTORY ENROLLMENT IS THE TERMINAL'S FIRST STAGE (KLD-2026-09-03-
FACTORY-ENROLLMENT-001). The image carries the bootstrap runtime only:
identity, cloud registration, health, update, host keys and a status
screen. It carries NO Store authority of any kind -- no Hub agent, no
database, no business application -- and the `retired` list below is
asserted absent by every test that reads this file.
NOTHING PER-DEVICE BELONGS IN AN IMAGE. No device key, certificate, tenant,
store, location, staff record, machine-id or SSH host key is declared here.
Factory Enrollment. The device announces itself and waits for an
explicit Admin approval; no answer on this path makes it `enrolled`.
Clone hygiene, second half: the image ships no host keys, so a per-device
set is generated at first boot from the distribution's ssh-keygen.
DEFINED, NO LONGER ENABLED. The tty1 text screen: device id, KitLuy
registration state, Store always Unassigned. It takes NO INPUT, and the
provisioning model needs a human to type a pairing code — so the graphical
Device Shell replaced it as the display owner (see `tty1` below). Kept in
the image as the recovery surface: it needs no compositor, no GPU and no
Electron, so it still works on a board where the shell cannot start.
THE DISPLAY OWNER. The graphical first-boot surface: registration state,
and once HET approves the board, the keypad that takes an eight-character
pairing code. Runs under `cage` — a kiosk compositor that shows exactly one
application with no desktop behind it — because a general compositor on a
shop counter is a way out of the application.
Carries no Store authority and offers no path to a business application
before activation (owner decision v2.0.0 4-5).
PINNED EXTERNAL BINARY, not committed. Debian ships no Electron, and 289 MB
of somebody else's binary does not belong in every clone — so it is acquired
the way rpi-image-gen itself is: a pinned version plus the checksum of the
exact artifact, fetched and VERIFIED by scripts/fetch-electron.sh and
installed by the layer. It is therefore invisible to the overlay
cross-check and is asserted against the BUILT rootfs instead.
`version` must equal the `electron` devDependency of the shell app: an image
and an app that disagree about the runtime is the defect the pin prevents.
Defined, NOT enabled. The Wayland session unit stays in the image as the
declared successor of the text screen on tty1, and is switched on by the
Device Shell slice, not before: it failed on the first real terminal boot
(2026-08-13) because nothing existed for the compositor to show.
GOVERNED APPLICATION RELEASE (KLD-2026-08-11-DEVICE-BOOTSTRAP-RUNTIME-001).
The unit is defined so the release need not invent one, and carries no
executable here: the business application is never part of the image.

retired.reason: The flash-time ticket path enrolled a device straight to `enrolled` with no Admin decision, which the Factory Enrollment rule forbids; its identity also included the SD card. Cloud registration is the terminal's one identity path.

tty1.$comment: Flipped by the Device Shell slice (2026-09-07). The successor recorded here was kitluy-terminal-session.service, and it is NOT what took the display: that unit runs labwc around a TEXT program, which is why the first real terminal showed a blank screen (2026-08-13). It stays in the image, still not enabled, for the governed POS release that genuinely needs a general compositor. The owner is the cage kiosk, and kitluy-bootstrap-screen.service remains defined as the no-GPU recovery surface.
